_about: How every route that takes a resource id is scoped to a tenant: the ONE registry for
id-addressed routes (tests/test_tenancy_route_scoping.py; the old matrix's id loop is gone).
One entry per 'METHOD path' of tests/fixtures/rbac_route_permissions.json that has a path parameter.
scope=workspace: the id names a resource owned by one workspace. The suite seeds one in
workspace A and calls the route as B's administrator, as B's API key and (unless a GET) as a
viewer of A who edits B with no workspace header: 404/403, nothing of A's in the body, and A's
resource unchanged. Owner control: A's own administrator must get a different answer, or
'owner_control_reason' says why that cannot be shown. 'viewer_may_call' (with a reason) lets a
viewer of the owning workspace call a route that changes nothing.
scope=platform: deployment-wide configuration, account or workspace lifecycle administration.
The same callers (none a platform administrator) are refused and nothing changes.
scope=exempt: the parameter is not a tenant-owned resource; 'reason' says why.
_body_routes_about: body_routes: mutating routes that take a resource id in the request BODY (no path parameter). Each needs a case in tests/test_tenancy_route_scoping.py::_BODY_ROUTE_BODIES: B is refused for A's ids and A's administrator is served (owner control).
